target: Two different sets of bracts on the fig (syconium, FLOPO_0986130). 'sans bractées externes' is about lateral/outer bracts on the fig wall: bract (PO_0009055) absent (PATO_0000462), limited to lateral/outer bracts. 'bractées basilaires connées' is about the basal bracts at the base of the fig: bract (PO_0009055) connate, limited to basal bracts. The words that tell them apart are 'externes' (outer/lateral) and 'basilaires' (basal).
fix: If a part name carries a position word ('bractées externes/latérales/basilaires/involucrales', 'outer/lateral/basal/inner bracts', 'outer tepals'), keep that word as a limit on the annotation. Then 'sans <part> <position word>' only rules out that subset, not the whole part. Do not check absence against presence for the same part when either side has a position word. In Ficus, 'bractées externes/latérales' on the fig and 'bractées basilaires' are separate sets.
reason: In Ficus descriptions, the fig (receptacle) is often described as 'sans bractées latérales/externes' while it still has 2–3 basal bracts, which are often connate. Both statements are true of the same fig. The contradiction only appears because both were mapped to plain 'bract'. Also, the absence statement is labelled 'bract: present', so the negation ('sans') was lost or the label is wrong. The absence should be checked too.

target: The outer surface of the fig: syconium (FLOPO_0986130) puberulous (FLOPO_0991049). If the fig is not yet allowed as a bearer, use fruit (PO_0009001) puberulous (FLOPO_0991049). It should not be bract.
fix: 'pubérulent(e) sur la face externe' / 'puberulous on the outer surface' has no subject of its own. It describes the organ that heads the current sentence or clause (here the fig/receptacle), not the nearest earlier part name. In particular, 'externe' in 'face externe' must not pick up 'bractées externes' from a nearby 'sans' clause. A part named only inside a 'sans/without' clause can never be the bearer of the qualities that follow it.
reason: 'Face externe' (outer surface) is the usual way Ficus descriptions describe hairs on the outside of the fig wall, as opposed to its inside. The only bracts named nearby are either stated as absent ('sans bractées externes') or are the basal bracts, so 'bract puberulous' comes from linking the hairs to the wrong part. Once it is moved to the fig, the contradiction goes away.
